title.zh: 卷十一 列傳第五 張弘策 庾域 鄭紹叔 呂僧珍
title.en: Volume 11: Zhang Hongce; Yu Yu; Zheng Shaoshu; Lü Sengzhen
title.raw: 卷十一 列傳第五 張弘策 庾域 鄭紹叔 呂僧珍 Volume 11: Zhang Hongce; Yu Yu; Zheng Shaoshu; Lü Sengzhen

sentences.zh: 張弘策

translations.literal: Zhang Hongce
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongce

sentences.zh: 張弘策，字真簡，范陽方城人，文獻皇后之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, was a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang, a younger cousin on his mother's side of Empress Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, came from Fangcheng in Fanyang—a maternal cousin of Empress Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 幼以孝聞。

translations.literal: From childhood he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 母嘗有疾，五日不食，弘策亦不食。

translations.literal: Once when his mother fell ill, for five days she would not eat, and Hongce would not eat either.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill she refused food for five days, and Hongce refused food as well.

sentences.zh: 母強爲進粥，乃食母所餘。

translations.literal: His mother forced him to take gruel; only then did he eat what she had left.
translations.idiomatic: She made him swallow porridge; he ate only what remained of hers.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，三年不食鹽菜，幾至滅性。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother, for three years he ate neither salt nor vegetables, nearly to the point of destroying his life.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his mother he took no salt or greens for three years, almost to death.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友愛，不忍暫離，雖各有室，常同臥起，世比之姜肱兄弟。

translations.literal: The brothers were affectionate and could not bear brief separation; though each had his own household, they often slept and rose together, and the age compared them to the Jiang Gong brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers loved one another and hated to part even briefly; though each had a home, they usually slept and rose together—the age likened them to the Jiang Gong brothers.

sentences.zh: 起家齊邵陵王國常侍，遷奉朝請、西中郎江夏王行參軍。

translations.literal: He first entered office as Attendant of the Prince of Shaoling's kingdom in Qi, and was transferred to Court Attendant and Acting Staff Officer to the Western Zhonglang General, Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an attendant in Qi's Prince of Shaoling kingdom, then became court attendant and acting staff officer to the Western Zhonglang General, Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 弘策與高祖年相輩，幼見親狎，恒隨高祖游處。

translations.literal: Hongce was of an age with Gaozu; from youth they were intimate, and he constantly followed Gaozu in his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce was Gaozu's contemporary; as youths they were close, and Hongce was always at Gaozu's side.

sentences.zh: 每入室，常覺有雲煙氣，體輒肅然，弘策由此特敬高祖。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered a room he would feel as though cloud and mist were present; his person would at once grow solemn, and from this Hongce came to hold Gaozu in special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he stepped into a room he seemed to sense cloud and mist; his bearing turned grave, and from that he revered Gaozu the more.

sentences.zh: 建武末，弘策從高祖宿，酒酣，徙席星下，語及時事。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu, Hongce kept overnight with Gaozu; when wine was deep they moved their mats under the stars and spoke of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu, Hongce lodged with Gaozu; drunk, they shifted their seats beneath the stars and talked of the age.

sentences.zh: 弘策因問高祖曰：「緯象云何？

translations.literal: Hongce then asked Gaozu: "What do the celestial signs say?
translations.idiomatic: Hongce asked Gaozu, "What do the omens say?

sentences.zh: 國家故當無恙？

translations.literal: Will the state in fact be unharmed?
translations.idiomatic: Will the realm truly be safe?

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「其可言乎？

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "Can that be spoken?
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "Can such things be said aloud?

sentences.zh: 」弘策因曰：「請言其兆。

translations.literal: " Hongce said: "Please speak the omens.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongce said, "Then tell me the signs.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「漢北有失地氣，浙東有急兵祥。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "North of Han there is an omen of lost territory; east of Zhe there is an omen of urgent arms.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "North of the Han the land will slip away; east of Zhe urgent armies will rise.

sentences.zh: 今冬初，魏必動；

translations.literal: This coming early winter Wei is certain to move;
translations.idiomatic: Early this winter Wei will surely stir;

sentences.zh: 若動則亡漢北。

translations.literal: if it moves, the north of Han will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: and if it moves, the north of Han is gone.

sentences.zh: 帝今久疾，多異議，萬一伺釁，稽部且乘機而作，是亦無成，徒自驅除耳。

translations.literal: The emperor is now long ill, and many dissenting voices are heard; should anyone seize the chance, the Kuaiji region too will rise—but it will accomplish nothing, only drive men to destroy one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has been ill long, and talk runs every way; if someone seizes the moment, Kuaiji may rise too—yet it will win nothing, only purge itself in vain.

sentences.zh: 明年都邑有亂，死人過於亂麻，齊之歷數，自茲亡矣。

translations.literal: Next year the capital will know disorder; the dead will outnumber tangled hemp; Qi's allotted span ends here.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the capital will fall into chaos; corpses will outnumber knotted hemp; Qi's fate ends with this.

sentences.zh: 梁、楚、漢當有英雄興。

translations.literal: Liang, Chu, and Han will see heroes rise.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, Chu, and Han heroes will rise.

sentences.zh: 」弘策曰：「英雄今何在？

translations.literal: " Hongce said: "Where is the hero now?
translations.idiomatic: " Hongce said, "Where is that hero now?

sentences.zh: 爲已富貴，爲在草茅？

translations.literal: Already in wealth and rank, or still in the thatched hut?
translations.idiomatic: Already rich and honored, or still in the grass?

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑曰：「光武有云：『安知非僕』。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed and said: "Guangwu once said, 'How do you know it is not I?'
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu laughed. "Guangwu said, 'How do you know it is not me?'

sentences.zh: 」弘策起曰：「今夜之言，是天意也。

translations.literal: " Hongce rose and said: "Tonight's words are Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongce stood. "Tonight's speech is Heaven's decree.

sentences.zh: 請定君臣之分。

translations.literal: Please fix lord and minister's roles.
translations.idiomatic: Let us settle lord and minister now.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「舅欲效鄧晨乎？

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "Uncle, do you wish to imitate Deng Chen?
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "Uncle—do you mean to play Deng Chen?

sentences.zh: 」是冬，魏軍寇新野，高祖將兵爲援，且受密旨，仍代曹虎爲雍州。

translations.literal: That winter Wei troops raided Xinye; Gaozu led an army in relief and, on a secret order, replaced Cao Hu as inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wei struck Xinye; Gaozu marched to relieve it and, on secret orders, took Yongzhou in place of Cao Hu.

sentences.zh: 弘策聞之心喜，謂高祖曰：「夜中之言，獨當驗矣。

translations.literal: Hongce heard it with joy and told Gaozu: "The words of that night should alone be proved.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce was delighted and told Gaozu, "What we said that night is about to come true.

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑曰：「且勿多言。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed and said: "For now, say no more.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu laughed. "Say no more—for now.

sentences.zh: 」弘策從高祖西行，仍參帷幄，身親軍役，不憚辛苦。

translations.literal: Hongce followed Gaozu west, still taking part in the command tent, personally sharing in campaigns and not shirking hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce followed Gaozu west, served in the command tent, and shared the hardships of every campaign.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，明帝崩，遺詔以高祖爲雍州刺史，乃表弘策爲錄事參軍，帶襄陽令。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year Mingdi died; the testamentary edict made Gaozu inspector of Yongzhou, and he memorialized Hongce as Recording Secretary and concurrent magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year five Mingdi died; by his final edict Gaozu became inspector of Yongzhou and named Hongce recording secretary with concurrent charge of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖睹海內方亂，有匡濟之心，密爲儲備，謀猷所及，惟弘策而已。

translations.literal: Gaozu saw the realm falling into disorder and bore a heart to set it right; he secretly made stores and laid plans—and in all of this only Hongce was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw chaos spread across the land and meant to rescue it; he stocked supplies in secret and weighed every plan with Hongce alone.

sentences.zh: 時長沙宣武王罷益州還，仍爲西中郎長史，行郢州事。

translations.literal: At the time the Xuanwu Prince of Changsha had left Yizhou and returned, and again served as Western Zhonglang long-term staff officer with acting charge of Ying province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanwu Prince of Changsha had just left Yizhou and again held the Western Zhonglang long-term staff post, acting for Ying province.

sentences.zh: 高祖使弘策到郢，陳計于宣武王，語在《高祖紀》。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Hongce to Ying to lay the plan before the Xuanwu Prince—the account is in the Annals of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Hongce to Ying to present the plan to the prince, as told in the Annals of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 弘策因說王曰：「昔周室旣衰，諸侯力爭，齊桓蓋中人耳，遂能一匡九合，民到于今稱之。

translations.literal: Hongce then urged the prince: "When the Zhou house had declined, the feudal lords strove for power; Duke Huan of Qi was only a middling man, yet he was able to unite the realm in nine gatherings, and the people to this day praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce urged the prince, "When Zhou waned, lords fought for power; Duke Huan of Qi was no more than an ordinary man, yet he united the realm nine times, and men still praise him.

sentences.zh: 齊德告微，四海方亂，蒼生之命，會應有主。

translations.literal: Qi's virtue is nearly spent; the four seas are in disorder; the fate of the living must find its lord.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's virtue is spent; the four seas are in turmoil; the people must have their ruler.

sentences.zh: 以郢州居中流之要，雍部有戎馬之饒，卿兄弟英武，當今無敵，虎據兩州，參分天下，糾合義兵，爲百姓請命，廢昏立明，易於反掌。

translations.literal: Ying province stands at the heart of the midstream; Yong holds horses in abundance; you and your brother are heroic and unmatched today—tiger-like over two provinces, you may divide the realm, gather righteous troops, plead for the people, cast down the benighted and raise the enlightened: it is easier than turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Ying lies at the midstream's hinge; Yong is rich in war-horses; you and your brother are heroes without peer—hold two provinces like tigers, split the realm, raise righteous arms, plead for the people, topple the dark and set up the bright: as easy as turning your palm.

sentences.zh: 如此，則桓、文之業可成，不世之功可建。

translations.literal: Thus the work of Huan and Wen may be achieved, and an unworldly merit established.
translations.idiomatic: Do that, and the deeds of Huan and Wen are yours, and glory beyond the age is within reach.

sentences.zh: 無爲豎子所欺，取笑身後。

translations.literal: Do not be duped by a petty fellow and become a laughingstock after death.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let some stripling fool you and make you a jest in later ages.

sentences.zh: 雍州揣之已熟，願善圖之。

translations.literal: Yongzhou has weighed this to the full; I beg you to plan well.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou has thought this through; plan wisely.

sentences.zh: 」王頗不懌而無以拒也。

translations.literal: " The prince was quite displeased yet had no way to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince was ill pleased but could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 義師將起，高祖夜召弘策、呂僧珍入宅定議，旦乃發兵，以弘策爲輔國將軍、軍主，領萬人督後部軍事。

translations.literal: When the righteous army was about to rise, Gaozu at night summoned Hongce and Lü Sengzhen to his house to fix the plan; at dawn he sent out the troops, making Hongce Supporting State General and army commander, commanding ten thousand men to supervise rear-area military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As the righteous army gathered, Gaozu called Hongce and Lü Sengzhen to his house by night to settle the plan; at dawn he marched, making Hongce Supporting State general and army commander over ten thousand men in charge of the rear.

sentences.zh: 西臺建，爲步兵校尉，遷車騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Western Headquarters was established, he was made Colonel of Foot Soldiers and transferred to Cavalry and Chariots Advisory Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the western headquarters was set up, he became colonel of foot soldiers, then cavalry and chariots advisory staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及郢城平，蕭穎達、楊公則諸將皆欲頓軍夏口，高祖以爲宜乘勢長驅，直指京邑，以計語弘策，弘策與高祖意合。

translations.literal: When Ying city was pacified, Xiao Yingda, Yang Gongze, and the other generals all wished to halt the army at Xiakou; Gaozu held that they should press the advantage in a long drive straight at the capital, and he spoke the plan to Hongce—Hongce agreed with Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying fell, Xiao Yingda and Yang Gongze wanted to camp at Xiakou; Gaozu meant to drive the victory straight to the capital and told Hongce, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 又訪寧遠將軍庾域，域又同。

translations.literal: He also consulted Pacify the Distant General Yu Yu; Yu too agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Pacify the Distant general Yu Yu, who agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 乃命衆軍卽日上道，沿江至建康，凡磯、浦、村落，軍行宿次、立頓處所，弘策逆爲圖測，皆在目中。

translations.literal: He then ordered the host to march that very day; along the river to Jiankang, every ford, harbor, and village—where the army halted, encamped, or pitched its posts—Hongce had mapped in advance, all within his eye.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the armies to march at once; from the river to Jiankang, every ford, beach, and hamlet where men camped or halted, Hongce had charted beforehand and held it all in mind.

sentences.zh: 義師至新林，王茂、曹景宗等於大航方戰，高祖遣弘策持節勞勉，衆咸奮厲。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Xinlin, Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong were fighting at the Great Crossing; Gaozu sent Hongce with staff insignia to encourage them, and the host was everywhere roused.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinlin, Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong fought at the Great Crossing; Gaozu sent Hongce with staff to hearten them, and all fought the harder.

sentences.zh: 是日，仍破朱雀軍。

translations.literal: That day they again broke the Vermilion Bird army.
translations.idiomatic: That same day they broke the Vermilion Bird force again.

sentences.zh: 高祖入頓石頭城，弘策屯門禁衛，引接士類，多全免。

translations.literal: Gaozu entered and encamped at Shitou city; Hongce garrisoned the gates in guard, received and guided men of rank, and many were wholly spared.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu encamped at Shitou; Hongce held the gates, received scholars and gentry, and saved many from harm.

sentences.zh: 城平，高祖遣弘策與呂僧珍先入清宮，封檢府庫。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, Gaozu sent Hongce and Lü Sengzhen ahead to clear the inner palace and seal and inspect the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Gaozu sent Hongce and Lü Sengzhen first into the inner palace to seal the treasuries.

sentences.zh: 于時城內珍寶委積，弘策申勒部曲，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: At the time treasures within the walls lay heaped; Hongce strictly warned his command, and not a hair was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures lay piled within the walls; Hongce forbade his men strictly, and nothing was touched.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉卿，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Guards, with additional appointment as Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commandant of the guards and also attendant within the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 天監初，加散騎常侍，洮陽縣侯，邑二千二百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was given additional title as Scattered Cavalry Attendant and Marquis of Taoyang county with a fief of two thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he was also made scattered cavalry attendant and marquis of Taoyang with two thousand two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 弘策盡忠奉上，知無不爲，交友故舊，隨才薦拔，搢紳皆趨焉。

translations.literal: Hongce gave loyal service above and knew nothing he would not do; with friends and old acquaintances he promoted each according to talent, and the gentry all flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce served with full loyalty and left nothing undone; he raised friends and old ties by their gifts, and the gentry gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 時東昏餘黨初逢赦令，多未自安，數百人因運荻炬束仗，得入南北掖作亂，燒神虎門、總章觀。

translations.literal: At the time the remnant partisans of Dong Hun had just received an amnesty and many were still uneasy; several hundred men, using reed transport, bundled torches and weapons, entered the Southern and Northern Side Gates to make trouble, burning Shenhu Gate and Zongzhang View.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun's remnant followers had just been pardoned and many still feared for their lives; several hundred, under cover of reed transport, smuggled torches and arms through the side gates, burned Shenhu Gate and Zongzhang View, and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 前軍司馬呂僧珍直殿內，以宿衛兵拒破之，盜分入衛尉府，弘策方救火，盜潛後害之，時年四十七。

translations.literal: Front Army Chief Clerk Lü Sengzhen was on duty within the palace and, with the night guard, repelled and broke them; the robbers split and entered the Commandant of the Guards' office—Hongce was then fighting the fire, and a robber stole behind and killed him, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Front army chief clerk Lü Sengzhen held the inner palace with the night guard and broke them; robbers slipped into the commandant's quarters while Hongce fought the blaze—a thief crept behind and killed him. He was forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 高祖深慟惜焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu mourned him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu grieved for him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 給第一區，衣一襲，錢十萬，布百匹，蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: He granted one residence in the first ward, one suit of clothes, one hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He granted a house in the first ward, a suit of robes, one hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「亡從舅衛尉，慮發所忽，殞身祅豎。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The late maternal uncle, Commandant of the Guards, was struck down in a moment of heedlessness by evil minions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "My late maternal uncle, commandant of the guards, was cut down in a careless hour by wicked men.

sentences.zh: 其情理清貞，器識淹濟，自籓升朝，契闊夷阻。

translations.literal: His reason and bearing were pure and upright, his talent and insight broad and deep; from the provinces he rose to court, sharing hardship through distant trials.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was clear and his conduct straight; his talent ran deep; from the provinces he came to court and shared every trial.

sentences.zh: 加外氏凋衰，饗嘗屢絕，興感《渭陽》，情寄斯在。

translations.literal: Moreover, on my mother's side the line had withered and sacrifices were often broken; stirred by the 'Wei-yang' ode, my feeling rested on him.
translations.idiomatic: My mother's kin had dwindled and rites were often broken; reading the Wei-yang, I fixed my heart on him.

sentences.zh: 方賴忠勳，翼宣寡薄，報效無徵，永言增慟。

translations.literal: I was about to rely on his loyal merit to support my slight virtue; he gave no sign of repayment, and my grief only grows.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to lean on his loyal service to shore my slender reign; he answered with no sign, and my sorrow deepens.

sentences.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Scattered Cavalry Attendant and General of Cavalry and Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him posthumously scattered cavalry attendant and general of cavalry and chariots.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Grant one suite of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Grant one suite of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 諡曰愍。」

translations.literal: Posthumous name Lamented."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Lamented."

sentences.zh: 弘策爲人寬厚通率，篤舊故。

translations.literal: Hongce by nature was generous, open, and direct, and deeply loyal to old ties.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce was generous, frank, and true to old friends.

sentences.zh: 及居隆重，不以貴勢自高。

translations.literal: Even when he stood in high and weighty office, he did not raise himself on wealth and power.
translations.idiomatic: Even in great office he never lorded it over others.

sentences.zh: 故人賓客，禮接如布衣時。

translations.literal: Old friends and guests he received with the same courtesy as in his days in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends and guests were welcomed as when he wore common cloth.

sentences.zh: 祿賜皆散之親友。

translations.literal: Salary and gifts he gave all away to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Stipends and gifts he scattered among kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 及其遇害，莫不痛惜焉。

translations.literal: When he met his violent end, none did not grieve for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was killed, all who knew him mourned.

sentences.zh: 子緬嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Mian succeeded; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mian succeeded him; his life is told elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 庾域，字司大，新野人。

translations.literal: Yu Yu
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu

sentences.zh: 長沙宣武王爲梁州，以爲錄事參軍，帶華陽太守。

translations.literal: Yu Yu, styled Sima Da, was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu, styled Sima Da, came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 時魏軍攻圍南鄭，州有空倉數十所，域封題指示將士云：「此中粟皆滿，足支二年，但努力堅守。

translations.literal: When the Xuanwu Prince of Changsha was in Liang province, he made Yu recording secretary and concurrent Administrator of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanwu Prince of Changsha held Liang province, he made Yu recording secretary and concurrent administrator of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 」衆心以安。

translations.literal: At the time Wei troops besieged Nanzheng; in the province were several dozen empty granaries; Yu sealed and labeled them and showed the troops, saying: "The grain here is all full—enough for two years; only strive to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei besieged Nanzheng; the province held dozens of empty granaries; Yu sealed them and told the troops, "Every bin is full—two years' grain. Hold fast.

sentences.zh: 虜退，以功拜羽林監，遷南中郎記室參軍。

translations.literal: " The host's heart was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The army took heart.

sentences.zh: 永元末，高祖起兵，遣書招域。

translations.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, by merit he was made Feathered Forest Commandant and transferred to Southern Zhonglang headquarters recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, he was made feathered forest commandant, then southern Zhonglang headquarters recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 西台建，以爲寧朔將軍，領行選，從高祖東下。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan, Gaozu raised the army and sent a letter summoning Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongyuan Gaozu rose in arms and wrote to summon Yu.

sentences.zh: 師次楊口，和帝遣御史中丞宗夬銜命勞軍。

translations.literal: When the Western Headquarters was established, he was made Pacify the North General with acting charge of selection and followed Gaozu east.
translations.idiomatic: When the western headquarters was set up, he was made pacify-the-north general with acting charge of selection and followed Gaozu east.

sentences.zh: 域乃諷夬曰：「黃鉞未加，非所以總率侯伯。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Yangkou, Emperor He sent Imperial Censor Zong Yun with orders to comfort the host.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangkou, Emperor He sent imperial censor Zong Yun to comfort the armies.

sentences.zh: 」夬反西臺，卽授高祖黃鉞。

translations.literal: Yu then urged Yun: "The yellow battle-ax has not yet been granted—this is not how one commands the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pressed Yun: "Without the yellow battle-ax you cannot command the lords.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎胄旣都督中外諸軍事，論者謂高祖應致牋，域爭不聽，乃止。

translations.literal: Yun returned to the Western Headquarters, and at once the yellow battle-ax was granted to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun went back to the western headquarters, and the yellow battle-ax was given to Gaozu at once.

sentences.zh: 郢城平。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yingzhou had been made area commander of all military affairs within and without, opinion held that Gaozu ought to submit a formal letter; Yu argued against it and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yingzhou became area commander of all armies, some said Gaozu should send a formal letter of submission; Yu objected and the idea was dropped.

sentences.zh: 域及張弘策議與高祖意合，卽命衆軍便下。

translations.literal: Ying city was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ying city fell.

sentences.zh: 每獻謀畫，多被納用。

translations.literal: Yu and Zhang Hongce debated in accord with Gaozu's intent, and the host was at once ordered to march downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Zhang Hongce argued as Gaozu wished, and the armies marched downstream at once.

sentences.zh: 霸府初開，以爲諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Whenever he offered a plan, it was often adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Plans he offered were usually taken.

sentences.zh: 天監初，封廣牧縣子，後軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the hegemon's headquarters first opened, he was made advisory staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the hegemon's headquarters opened, he became an advisory staff officer.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangmu and made Rear Army Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he was made viscount of Guangmu and rear army chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 梁州長史夏侯道遷舉州叛降魏，魏騎將襲巴西，域固守百餘日，城中糧盡，將士皆齕草食土，死者太半，無有離心。

translations.literal: He went out as Pacify the North General and Administrator of the two commanderies Brazil and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Brazil and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退，詔增封二百戶，進爵爲伯。

translations.literal: Liang province long-term staff officer Xiahou Daoyuan raised the province in rebellion and surrendered to Wei; Wei horsemen were about to strike Brazil; Yu held firm more than a hundred days; grain in the city was exhausted and officers and soldiers gnawed grass and ate earth—more than half died—yet none lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Daoyuan, Liang's long-term staff officer, rebelled and surrendered the province to Wei; Wei cavalry struck Brazil; Yu held more than a hundred days; grain ran out and men ate grass and earth—more than half died—yet none wavered.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒於郡。

translations.literal: When the Wei army withdrew, an edict added two hundred households to his fief and advanced his rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei withdrew, an edict added two hundred households to his fief and raised him to marquis.

sentences.zh: 鄭紹叔

translations.literal: Zheng Shaoshu
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shaoshu

sentences.zh: 鄭紹叔，字仲明，滎陽開封人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Shaoshu, styled Zhongming, was a native of Kaifeng in Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shaoshu, styled Zhongming, came from Kaifeng in Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 世居壽陽。

translations.literal: His clan for generations dwelt in Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 祖琨，宋高平太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kun was Song Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kun had been Song administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 紹叔少孤貧。

translations.literal: Shaoshu in youth was orphaned and poor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu was orphaned young and lived in poverty.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，爲安豊令，居縣有能名。

translations.literal: Past twenty years of age, he was magistrate of Anfeng; while in the county he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Past twenty he was magistrate of Anfeng and won a name for competence in the district.

sentences.zh: 本州召補主簿，轉治中從事史。

translations.literal: The province summoned him to fill chief clerk and he was transferred to supervising clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province called him to chief clerk, then made him supervising clerk.

sentences.zh: 時刺史蕭誕以弟諶誅，臺遣收兵卒至，左右莫不驚散，紹叔聞難，獨馳赴焉。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector Xiao Yan, because his younger brother Shen was executed, the court sent troops to seize him; those at hand were all startled and scattered, but Shaoshu, hearing of the crisis, alone galloped to him.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xiao Yan's younger brother Shen had been put to death; when court troops came to take Yan, his attendants fled in panic, but Shaoshu alone rode to him at the news.

sentences.zh: 誕死，侍送喪柩，衆咸稱之。

translations.literal: When Dan died, Shaoshu attended and escorted the coffin; all praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan died, Shaoshu escorted the coffin in person, and everyone praised him.

sentences.zh: 到京師，司空徐孝嗣見而異之，曰：「祖逖之流也。」

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi saw him and was struck, saying, "A man in the mold of Zu Ti."
translations.idiomatic: At the capital, Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi took notice and said, "This is Zu Ti's kind of man."

sentences.zh: 高祖臨司州，命爲中兵參軍，領長流，因是厚自結附。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took charge of Sizhou, he appointed Shaoshu Middle Army Aide, with charge of the long patrol, and from then on Shaoshu bound himself closely to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held Sizhou, he made Shaoshu Middle Army Aide in charge of the long patrol, and Shaoshu thereafter attached himself closely.

sentences.zh: 高祖罷州還京師，謝遣賓客，紹叔獨固請願留。

translations.literal: When Gaozu left the province and returned to the capital, he dismissed his guests with thanks; Shaoshu alone pressed hard to be allowed to stay.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu left the province for the capital and released his guests, Shaoshu alone insisted on remaining.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂曰：「卿才幸自有用，我今未能相益，宜更思他塗。

translations.literal: Gaozu said to him, "Your talent will surely find use; I cannot benefit you yet—you should seek another path."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told him, "Your talent will surely serve somewhere; I cannot help you yet. You should look elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」紹叔曰：「委質有在，義無二心。

translations.literal: Shaoshu said, "Having pledged myself, my loyalty admits no second heart."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu said, "I have pledged myself. My loyalty knows no second allegiance."

sentences.zh: 」高祖固不許，於是乃還壽陽。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly would not agree, and so Shaoshu returned to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu still refused, and Shaoshu went back to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 刺史蕭遙昌苦引紹叔，終不受命。

translations.literal: Inspector Xiao Yaochang pressed him hard to serve, but in the end Shaoshu would not accept the post.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xiao Yaochang pressed him repeatedly, yet Shaoshu never accepted command.

sentences.zh: 遙昌怒，將囚之，救解得免。

translations.literal: Yaochang grew angry and was about to imprison him; rescue and mediation won his release.
translations.idiomatic: Yaochang flew into a rage and meant to imprison him, but others intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 及高祖爲雍州刺史，紹叔間道西歸，補甯蠻長史、扶風太守。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Inspector of Yongzhou, Shaoshu came west by hidden routes and was appointed Chief of Ningman and Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took Yongzhou, Shaoshu stole west by back roads and was made Chief of Ningman and Administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 東昏旣害朝宰，頗疑高祖。

translations.literal: After Donghun had killed the chief ministers of state, he grew quite suspicious of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Donghun had slain the court's leading ministers, his suspicion of Gaozu deepened.

sentences.zh: 紹叔兄植爲東昏直後，東昏遣至雍州，託以候紹叔，實潛使爲刺客。

translations.literal: Shaoshu's elder brother Zhi served as Donghun's personal attendant in the rear palace; Donghun sent him to Yongzhou, ostensibly to visit Shaoshu, but in truth to set him on Gaozu as an assassin.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu's brother Zhi was Donghun's rear-palace attendant; Donghun sent him to Yongzhou under the pretense of visiting Shaoshu, while secretly ordering him to kill Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 紹叔知之，密以白高祖。

translations.literal: Shaoshu learned of it and secretly reported the matter to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu learned the plot and secretly told Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 植旣至，高祖于紹叔處置酒宴之，戲植曰：「朝廷遣卿見圖，今日閑宴，是見取良會也。

translations.literal: When Zhi arrived, Gaozu set wine for him at Shaoshu's quarters and jested with Zhi, saying, "The court sent you to plot against me. Today's idle feast is your best chance to take me."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi came, Gaozu feasted him at Shaoshu's house and said in jest, "The court sent you to kill me. This leisurely banquet is your finest opening."

sentences.zh: 」賓主大笑。

translations.literal: Host and guest laughed aloud together.
translations.idiomatic: Host and guest burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 令植登臨城隍，周觀府署，士卒、器械、舟艫、戰馬，莫不富實。

translations.literal: He had Zhi climb the city wall and look about the offices; soldiers, weapons, boats, and war-horses—nothing was not ample and strong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhi up on the ramparts to tour the compound: troops, arms, boats, and horses were all lavishly supplied.

sentences.zh: 植退謂紹叔曰：「雍州實力，未易圖也。

translations.literal: Zhi withdrew and said to Shaoshu, "Yongzhou's strength is not easily taken."
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, Zhi told Shaoshu, "Yongzhou is not a prize easily seized."

sentences.zh: 」紹叔曰：「兄還，具爲天子言之。

translations.literal: Shaoshu said, "Brother, when you return, tell the Son of Heaven everything plainly."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu said, "Go back and report all of this faithfully to the throne."

sentences.zh: 兄若取雍州，紹叔請以此衆一戰。

translations.literal: If brother means to take Yongzhou, I ask only to meet your host with these troops in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: If you come for Yongzhou, I will meet your army in open battle with these men.

sentences.zh: 」送兄于南峴，相持慟哭而別。

translations.literal: He saw his brother off at South Xian; they clung to each other and wept as they parted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his brother off at South Xian, and the two held each other, weeping, before they separated.

sentences.zh: 義師起，爲冠軍將軍，改驍騎將軍，侍從東下江州，留紹叔監州事，督江、湘二州糧運，事無闕乏。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, he was made General of the Champions, then changed to General of Valiant Cavalry; he followed east to Jiangzhou, while Shaoshu was left to oversee the province and supervise grain transport for Jiang and Xiang—nothing fell short.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, he became General of the Champions, then General of Valiant Cavalry, and marched east to Jiangzhou; Shaoshu stayed to govern the province and supply Jiang and Xiang with grain, without a single lapse.

sentences.zh: 天監初，入爲衛尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he entered the capital as Minister of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tianjian he entered court as Minister of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 紹叔忠於事上，外所聞知，纖毫無隱。

translations.literal: Shaoshu was loyal in serving his lord; of all he heard abroad, not the slightest thread was hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu served with absolute loyalty; whatever reached him from outside, he concealed nothing.

sentences.zh: 每爲高祖言事，善則曰：「臣愚不及，此皆聖主之策。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke to Gaozu of affairs, if they went well he said, "I am too dull to deserve credit; these are all the sagely lord's measures."
translations.idiomatic: When he reported good news to Gaozu, he said, "I am too dull for praise; this is the sagely lord's doing alone."

sentences.zh: 」其不善，則曰：「臣慮出淺短，以爲其事當如是，殆以此誤朝廷，臣之罪深矣。

translations.literal: If they went ill, he said, "My counsel was shallow; I thought the matter should be thus, and nearly misled the court thereby—my fault is grave."
translations.idiomatic: If matters went wrong, he said, "My judgment was shallow. I thought it should be done this way and nearly led the court astray. The fault is mine."

sentences.zh: 」高祖甚親信之。

translations.literal: Gaozu trusted and favored him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu cherished and relied on him utterly.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 紹叔有至性，高祖常使人節其哭。

translations.literal: Shaoshu's nature was utmost in filial piety; Gaozu often sent men to moderate his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu's filial devotion ran deep; Gaozu repeatedly sent attendants to restrain his grief.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起爲冠軍將軍、右軍司馬，封營道縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as General of the Champions and Right Army Major, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingdao with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned as General of the Champions and Right Army Major, enfeoffed Marquis of Yingdao with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 俄復爲衛尉卿，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was again Minister of the Guards, with the additional title General of the Champions.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon again Minister of the Guards, also bearing the rank General of the Champions.

sentences.zh: 以營道縣戶凋弊，改封東興縣侯，邑如故。

translations.literal: Because the households of Yingdao county were depleted and in distress, his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Dongxing, the fief remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: As Yingdao's households had withered, his title was shifted to Marquis of Dongxing, the fief unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，紹叔少失父，事母及祖母以孝聞，奉兄恭謹。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shaoshu had lost his father young; he served his mother and grandmother with a filial name, and toward his elder brother he was reverent and careful.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had lost his father; he was famed for honoring mother and grandmother, and deferential toward his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及居顯要，祿賜所得及四方貢遺，悉歸之兄室。

translations.literal: Once he stood in high office, his salary, gifts, and tribute from all quarters he sent entirely to his brother's household.
translations.idiomatic: In high rank, every stipend, gift, and tribute went straight to his brother's house.

sentences.zh: 三年，魏軍圍合肥，紹叔以本號督衆軍鎮東關，事平，復爲衛尉。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wei armies besieged Hefei; Shaoshu in his former title commanded the armies garrisoning Dong Pass. When the affair was settled, he again became Minister of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, Wei besieged Hefei; Shaoshu commanded the armies at Dong Pass. After peace returned, he was again Minister of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 旣而義陽爲魏所陷，司州移鎮關南。

translations.literal: Soon after, Yiyang fell to Wei, and Sizhou's seat was moved south of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yiyang fell to Wei, and the Sizhou headquarters shifted south of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 四年，以紹叔爲使持節、征虜將軍、司州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Shaoshu was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹叔創立城隍，繕修兵器，廣田積穀，招納流民，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Shaoshu raised walls and moats, repaired weapons, opened fields and stored grain, gathered in displaced people—the common folk found peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He built ramparts, sharpened arms, opened fields, hoarded grain, and received refugees until the people rested easy.

sentences.zh: 性頗矜躁，以權勢自居，然能傾心接物，多所薦舉，士類亦以此歸之。

translations.literal: By nature he was somewhat proud and quick-tempered, comporting himself as one who held power; yet he could give his heart to others and recommend many men, and the gentry for that reason rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was proud and quick-tempered, mindful of his power, yet open-handed in friendship and generous in recommendations, and scholars gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵爲左將軍，加通直散騎常侍，領司、豫二州大中正。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Left General, with the additional office Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of Si and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was recalled as Left General, also Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of Si and Yu.

sentences.zh: 紹叔至家疾篤。

translations.literal: When Shaoshu reached home his illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Shaoshu reached home, he was desperately ill.

sentences.zh: 詔於宅拜授，輿載還府，中使醫藥，一日數至。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him at his dwelling; he was carried back to his office in a litter, and palace envoys with medicine came several times in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The throne invested him at his house, had him borne back to office in a litter, and sent physicians from court several times a day.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒於府舍，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in his official residence, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he died at his government house, forty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 高祖將臨其殯，紹叔宅巷狹陋，不容輿駕，乃止。

translations.literal: Gaozu meant to attend his lying-in-state, but Shaoshu's lane and courtyard were too narrow for the imperial carriage, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wished to visit the bier, but Shaoshu's alley was too cramped for the imperial coach, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「追往念功，前王所篤；

translations.literal: The edict read: "To recall the dead and honor merit is what former kings held dear;
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "To honor the dead and reward merit is what former kings treasured;

sentences.zh: 在誠惟舊，異代同規。

translations.literal: to keep faith with the loyal across ages is the same rule in every time."
translations.idiomatic: to hold fast to old loyalty across ages is one law for every dynasty."

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍、東興縣開國侯紹叔，立身清正，奉上忠恪，契闊籓朝，情績顯著。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Right Guard General, and Marquis of Dongxing, Shaoshu, stood upright and pure in person, loyal and earnest in serving his lord; through long service at the frontier court his merit and feeling were plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Right Guard General, and founding Marquis of Dongxing, was upright in conduct and utterly loyal; from long service on the frontier his devotion and deeds shone clear.

sentences.zh: 爰及義始，寔立茂勳，作牧疆境，效彰所莅。

translations.literal: From the righteous beginning he truly raised lofty achievement; as shepherd of the borderlands the good he wrought where he ruled was manifest.
translations.idiomatic: From the first rising of the righteous cause he won great merit; governing the marches, his achievements where he served were evident.

sentences.zh: 方申任寄，協贊心膂；

translations.literal: He was just then to receive further trust and share in the work of the heart and backbone;
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of greater trust, to stand at the ruler's right hand;

sentences.zh: 奄至殞喪，傷痛於懷。

translations.literal: suddenly he fell to death and ruin, and grief pierced the breast."
translations.idiomatic: when suddenly he fell—grief cuts to the bone."

sentences.zh: 宜加優典，隆茲寵命。

translations.literal: He should receive added honors and this exalted bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Let him receive added honors and this lofty posthumous grace.

sentences.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、護軍將軍，給鼓吹一部，東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，凶事所須，隨由資給。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards, with one set of martial music, Eastern Garden secret rites, one court robe, one suit of garments, and whatever the funeral requires supplied as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously: Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards, with martial music, Eastern Garden rites, court robes, a full suit, and whatever the funeral demands supplied at need.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠。」

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal."
translations.idiomatic: His temple name was Loyal."

sentences.zh: 紹叔卒後，高祖嘗潸然謂朝臣曰：「鄭紹叔立志忠烈，善則稱君，過則歸己，當今殆無其比。

translations.literal: After Shaoshu's death, Gaozu once said tearfully to the court, "Zheng Shaoshu set his will on loyal fierceness; when things went well he praised his lord, when they went ill he took the blame on himself—today there is scarcely his equal."
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoshu died, Gaozu once told the court through tears, "Zheng Shaoshu lived for loyalty; in success he praised his lord, in failure he blamed himself. I doubt we shall see his like again."

sentences.zh: 」其見賞惜如此。

translations.literal: Such was the measure of his esteem and regret.
translations.idiomatic: So deeply was he valued and mourned.

sentences.zh: 子貞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhen inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 呂僧珍

translations.literal: Lü Sengzhen
translations.idiomatic: Lü Sengzhen

sentences.zh: 呂僧珍，字元瑜，東平范人也。

translations.literal: Lü Sengzhen, style name Yuanyu, was a native of Fan in Dongping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Sengzhen, styled Yuanyu, came from Fan in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 世居廣陵。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had lived in Guangling for generations.

sentences.zh: 起自寒賤。

translations.literal: He rose from cold poverty.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from humble want.

sentences.zh: 始童兒時，從師學，有相工歷觀諸生，指僧珍謂博士曰：「此有奇聲，封侯相也。

translations.literal: As a boy, when he followed his teacher in study, a physiognomist surveyed all the pupils and, pointing at Sengzhen, told the master, "This one has an extraordinary voice; he has the look of one enfeoffed."
translations.idiomatic: Still a boy at his teacher's school, a physiognomist reviewed the pupils, pointed at Sengzhen, and told the master, "That voice is not ordinary. He has the bearing of a man who will be enfeoffed."

sentences.zh: 」年二十餘，依宋丹陽尹劉秉，秉誅後，事太祖文皇爲門下書佐。

translations.literal: Past twenty, he attached himself to Song's Administrator of Danyang, Liu Bing; after Bing was executed, he served the founding Emperor Wen as a clerk in the Secretariat gate.
translations.idiomatic: Past twenty he served Song's Danyang administrator Liu Bing; after Bing's death he entered the founding Emperor Wen's gate as a Secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺五寸，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet five inches; his bearing was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He was seven feet five inches tall, with a commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 在同類中少所褻狎，曹輩皆敬之。

translations.literal: Among his peers he seldom treated anyone lightly; his colleagues all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Among equals he rarely indulged in familiarity; his fellows all honored him.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲豫州刺史，以爲典籤，帶蒙令，居官稱職。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor was Inspector of Yuzhou, he made Sengzhen Master of Documents with concurrent charge of Mengling, and in office he answered his post.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor held Yuzhou, he made Sengzhen Master of Documents and concurrent Magistrate of Mengling, and he performed well.

sentences.zh: 太祖遷領軍，補主簿。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor moved to command the guards, Sengzhen was appointed chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took command of the guards, Sengzhen became chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 妖賊唐瑀寇東陽，太祖率衆東討，使僧珍知行軍衆局事。

translations.literal: When the sorcerer-rebel Tang Yu raided Dongyang, the founding emperor led troops east to attack and had Sengzhen oversee the army's bureau of affairs on the march.
translations.idiomatic: When the sorcerer rebel Tang Yu struck Dongyang, the founding emperor marched east and put Sengzhen in charge of the army's marching bureau.

sentences.zh: 僧珍宅在建陽門東，自受命當行，每日由建陽門道，不過私室，太祖益以此知之。

translations.literal: Sengzhen's house lay east of the Jianyang Gate; from the day he took the commission to march, each day his route passed the Jianyang Gate road and never turned in at his private quarters—the founding emperor trusted him all the more for it.
translations.idiomatic: His home stood east of Jianyang Gate; from the day he was ordered out, his road passed the gate daily and never turned homeward, and the founding emperor prized him the more.

sentences.zh: 爲丹陽尹，復命爲郡督郵。

translations.literal: When he became Administrator of Danyang, he was again ordered to be the commandery's chief postal inspector.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Danyang he was again made the commandery's chief postal inspector.

sentences.zh: 齊隨王子隆出爲荊州刺史，齊武以僧珍爲子隆防閤，從之鎮。

translations.literal: When Qi's Prince of Sui, Zilong, went out as Inspector of Jingzhou, Qi Wudi made Sengzhen his guard captain and he followed to the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi's Prince of Sui Zilong went to Jing as inspector, Qi Wudi made Sengzhen his guard captain on the march to the province.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，雍州刺史王奐反，敕遣僧珍隸平北將軍曹虎西爲典籤，帶新城令。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming, Inspector of Yongzhou Wang Huan rebelled; an edict sent Sengzhen under the Pacifying-the-North General Cao Hu west as Master of Documents, with concurrent charge of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year nine, Yongzhou inspector Wang Huan rebelled; Sengzhen was sent west under Pacifying-the-North General Cao Hu as Master of Documents, with concurrent magistracy of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 魏軍寇沔北，司空陳顯達出討，一見異之，因屏人呼上座，謂曰：「卿有貴相，後當不見減，努力爲之。」

translations.literal: When Wei armies raided north of the Mian, Minister of Works Chen Xianda went out to attack; at first sight he was struck and, dismissing others, called Sengzhen to the upper seat and said, "You have a noble countenance; later you will not diminish—strive hard."
translations.idiomatic: When Wei raided north of the Mian, Minister of Works Chen Xianda took the field; at first meeting he was astonished, dismissed the room, seated Sengzhen above, and said, "You bear a noble face. Your later days will not fade. Drive yourself."

sentences.zh: 建武二年，魏大舉南侵，五道並進。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei launched a great southern invasion on five routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year two, Wei invaded south on a great scale, five armies advancing together.

sentences.zh: 高祖率師援義陽，僧珍從在軍中。

translations.literal: Gaozu led troops to relieve Yiyang; Sengzhen followed in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu marched to relieve Yiyang, and Sengzhen went with the host.

sentences.zh: 長沙宣武王時爲梁州刺史。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha, Xuanwu King, was then Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changsha, the Xuanwu King, then held Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏圍守連月，間諜所在不通，義陽與雍州路斷。

translations.literal: Wei besieged for months on end; spies could not pass anywhere, and the road between Yiyang and Yongzhou was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Wei besieged month after month; no spy could get through, and the road from Yiyang to Yongzhou was severed.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲遣使至襄陽，求梁州問，衆皆憚，莫敢行，僧珍固請充使，卽日單舸上道。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to send an envoy to Xiangyang to seek word of Liangzhou; all feared the journey and none dared go, but Sengzhen pressed to go as envoy and that very day set out alone in a single boat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu meant to send someone to Xiangyang for news of Liangzhou; all shrank from the road, but Sengzhen insisted and that same day sailed alone upstream.

sentences.zh: 旣至襄陽，督遣援軍，且獲宣武王書而反，高祖甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Once he reached Xiangyang he hurried the relief armies and also obtained the Xuanwu King's letter before returning; Gaozu praised him highly.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he drove the relief forces, secured the Xuanwu King's letter, and returned; Gaozu commended him in the highest terms.

sentences.zh: 事寧，補羽林監。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he was made Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，司空徐孝嗣管朝政，欲與共事，僧珍揣不久安，竟弗往。

translations.literal: When Donghun took the throne, Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi managed court affairs and wished to work with him; Sengzhen judged that security would not last and in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Donghun succeeded, Xu Xiaosi ran the government and sought his help; Sengzhen guessed the ground would not hold and never went.

sentences.zh: 時高祖已臨雍州，僧珍固求西歸，得補邔令。

translations.literal: By then Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen pressed hard to return west and was appointed Magistrate of Zou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen begged to go west and was made Magistrate of Zou.

sentences.zh: 旣至，高祖命爲中兵參軍，委以心膂。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Gaozu appointed him Middle Army Aide and entrusted him as heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Gaozu made him Middle Army Aide and trusted him as his right hand.

sentences.zh: 僧珍陰養死士，歸之者甚衆。

translations.literal: Sengzhen secretly nurtured men willing to die for him; those who came to him were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen quietly gathered men who would die for him, and a great host rallied.

sentences.zh: 高祖頗招武猛，士庶響從，會者萬餘人，因命按行城西空地，將起數千間屋，以爲止舍，多伐材竹，沈於檀溪，積茅蓋若山阜，皆不之用。

translations.literal: Gaozu gathered many fierce fighters; scholars and commoners answered the call, and those who assembled were more than ten thousand. He therefore ordered a survey of open ground west of the city wall, intending to raise several thousand rooms as lodging, felling much timber and bamboo and sinking it in the Tanxi, heaping thatch in mounds like hills—all unused.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drew fierce fighters until more than ten thousand gathered; he had the open ground west of the wall surveyed for thousands of lodgings, cut timber and bamboo and sank it in Tan Creek, and piled thatch into hillocks—yet used none of it.

sentences.zh: 僧珍獨悟其旨，亦私具櫓數百張。

translations.literal: Sengzhen alone grasped the intent and on his own also prepared several hundred oars.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen alone understood the plan and privately stockpiled hundreds of oars.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，高祖夜召僧珍及張弘策定議，明旦乃會衆發兵，悉取檀溪材竹，裝爲艛艦，葺之以茅，並立辦。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Gaozu summoned Sengzhen and Zhang Hongce by night to fix the plan; at dawn he mustered the host and marched, taking all the Tanxi timber and bamboo, fitting it as war-boats and thatching them with straw—everything ready at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Gaozu called Sengzhen and Zhang Hongce at night to decide; at dawn the host moved out, pulled up the Tanxi timber and bamboo, rigged them as warships roofed with thatch, and had all in an instant.

sentences.zh: 衆軍將發，諸將果爭櫓，僧珍乃出先所具者，每船付二張，爭者乃息。

translations.literal: As the armies were about to march, the generals indeed quarreled over oars; Sengzhen then produced those he had prepared beforehand, giving two to each boat, and the quarrel ceased.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies prepared to sail, the generals fought over oars; Sengzhen brought out his hidden store, two oars per vessel, and the dispute died.

sentences.zh: 高祖以僧珍爲輔國將軍、步兵校尉，出入臥內，宣通意旨。

translations.literal: Gaozu made Sengzhen Supporting-the-State General and Colonel of the Footmen; he went in and out of the sleeping quarters, conveying the lord's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made him Supporting-the-State General and Colonel of Footmen, entering the inner quarters to speak the ruler's mind.

sentences.zh: 師及郢城，僧珍率所領頓偃月壘，俄又進據騎城。

translations.literal: When the army reached Ying city, Sengzhen led his command to camp at the Crescent Fortress; soon after he advanced and seized Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Ying, Sengzhen encamped his men at Crescent Fortress, then pressed forward and took Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 郢州平，高祖進僧珍爲前鋒大將軍。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou was pacified, Gaozu advanced Sengzhen to Grand General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying fell, Gaozu promoted him to Grand General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 大軍次江寧，高祖令僧珍與王茂率精兵先登赤鼻邏。

translations.literal: The great host halted at Jiangning; Gaozu ordered Sengzhen and Wang Mao to lead picked troops to seize the Red Nose Ford first.
translations.idiomatic: The army stopped at Jiangning; Gaozu sent Sengzhen and Wang Mao with elite troops to take Red Nose Ford first.

sentences.zh: 其日，東昏將李居士與衆來戰，僧珍等要擊，大破之。

translations.literal: That day, Donghun's general Li Jushi came with his host to fight; Sengzhen and the others intercepted and broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: That day Donghun's general Li Jushi brought his force to battle; Sengzhen intercepted and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 乃與茂進軍于白板橋築壘，壘立，茂移頓越城，僧珍獨守白板。

translations.literal: Then he and Mao advanced to Whiteboard Bridge and raised a fortress; once the ramparts stood, Mao moved his camp to Yuecheng while Sengzhen alone held Whiteboard.
translations.idiomatic: He and Mao pushed to Whiteboard Bridge and built a fort; when it stood, Mao shifted to Yuecheng and Sengzhen held Whiteboard alone.

sentences.zh: 李居士密覘知衆少，率銳卒萬人，直來薄城。

translations.literal: Li Jushi secretly reconnoitered and knew the defenders were few; he led ten thousand crack troops and came straight to press the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jushi spied and saw how thin the garrison was; he led ten thousand elite men straight against the walls.

sentences.zh: 僧珍謂將士曰：「今力旣不敵，不可與戰；

translations.literal: Sengzhen told his officers and men, "Our strength cannot match them now; we must not give battle;
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen told the troops, "We are too few to fight them head-on;

sentences.zh: 亦勿遙射，須至塹裏，當並力破之。

translations.literal: nor shoot at them from afar—wait until they reach the moat, then strike with combined force and break them."
translations.idiomatic: and we must not loose arrows from afar. When they reach the ditch, we break them together."

sentences.zh: 」俄而皆越塹拔柵，僧珍分人上城，矢石俱發，自率馬步三百人出其後，守隅者復踰城而下，內外齊擊，居士應時奔散，獲其器甲不可勝計。

translations.literal: Before long they all crossed the ditch and tore up the palisade; Sengzhen sent men up on the wall, stones and arrows flying together, while he himself led three hundred horse and foot out behind them; the defenders on the corners also leaped down from the wall, and inner and outer struck together—Jushi scattered at once, and captured arms and armor beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they crossed the moat and wrenched down the stakes; Sengzhen put men on the wall with stones and arrows raining, led three hundred horse and foot around their rear, and had the corner guards leap down as well—inner and outer struck as one, Jushi fled instantly, and arms taken were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 僧珍又進據越城。

translations.literal: Sengzhen again advanced and seized Yuecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen pressed on and took Yuecheng.

sentences.zh: 東昏大將王珍國列車爲營，背淮而陣。

translations.literal: Donghun's great general Wang Zhenguo drew up chariots as camps, with their backs to the Huai in battle array.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun's great general Wang Zhenguo formed chariot encampments with his back to the Huai.

sentences.zh: 王茂等衆軍擊之，僧珍縱火車焚其營。

translations.literal: Wang Mao and the other hosts attacked; Sengzhen sent fire-chariots to burn their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao and the allied armies struck; Sengzhen rolled fire-chariots against the camps and burned them.

sentences.zh: 卽日瓦解。

translations.literal: That same day the enemy lines collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the enemy host dissolved.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，高祖命僧珍率所領先入清宮，與張弘策封檢府庫，卽日以本官帶南彭城太守，遷給事黃門侍郎，領虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Gaozu ordered Sengzhen to lead his troops first into the inner palace; with Zhang Hongce he sealed and inspected the treasury. That same day he kept his current post as acting Administrator of Nan Pengcheng, was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, and concurrently Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry of the Tiger guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Gaozu had Sengzhen lead his men first into the inner palace; with Zhang Hongce he sealed and checked the treasury. That day he kept his rank as acting Nan Pengcheng administrator, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, and held the Tiger guards colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，以爲冠軍將軍、前軍司馬，封平固縣侯，邑一千二百戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was made Champion General and front army marshal, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinggu district with a fief of twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Champion General and front army marshal, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinggu with twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋遷給事中、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attending Within and Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Attending Within and Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉左衛將軍，加散騎常侍，入直秘書省，總知宿衛。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Guard General, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, entered regular duty at the Secretariat, and had overall charge of palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Left Guard General, was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, took regular duty in the Secretariat, and oversaw the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 天監四年冬，大舉北伐，自是軍機多事，僧珍晝直中書省，夜還秘書。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Tianjian a great northern campaign was launched; from then on military affairs multiplied, and Sengzhen by day was on duty at the Central Secretariat and by night returned to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Tianjian year 4 the court launched a major northern campaign; military business piled up, and Sengzhen spent his days at the Central Secretariat and his nights back at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，又命僧珍率羽林勁勇出梁城。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year he was again ordered to lead elite Feathered Forest troops out from Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year 5 he was again ordered to lead crack Feathered Forest troops from Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 其年冬旋軍，以本官領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: That winter the army returned; he kept his current post and was made concurrent Crown Prince's Assistant in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the army came home; he kept his post and was made concurrent crown prince's assistant in the palace.

sentences.zh: 僧珍去家久，表求拜墓。

translations.literal: Sengzhen had been away from home long and submitted a memorial asking to visit his ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Long away from home, Sengzhen petitioned to visit his family graves.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲榮之，使爲本州，乃授使持節、平北將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to honor him and made him governor of his native province, granting him Bearer of the Staff with credentials, General Who Pacifies the North, and Southern Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu meant to honor him with his home province and appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Southern Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 僧珍在任，平心率下，不私親戚。

translations.literal: In office Sengzhen treated subordinates fairly and showed no favor to kin.
translations.idiomatic: In office Sengzhen was even-handed with subordinates and never favored relatives.

sentences.zh: 從父兄子先以販蔥爲業，僧珍旣至，乃棄業欲求州官。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother's son had earlier made his living selling scallions; when Sengzhen arrived, he abandoned the trade to seek a provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: A son of his father's elder brother had sold scallions for a living; when Sengzhen came to the province, the man quit the trade to seek an official post.

sentences.zh: 僧珍曰：「吾荷國重恩，無以報效，汝等自有常分，豈可妄求叨越，但當速反蔥肆耳。

translations.literal: Sengzhen said: "I bear the state's heavy grace and have no means to repay it; you each have your proper station—how can you rashly seek to overstep? You should quickly return to the scallion shop.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen said, "I owe the state a heavy debt I cannot repay; you each have your proper place—how can you seek promotion rashly? Go back to your scallion stall at once.

sentences.zh: 」僧珍舊宅在市北，前有督郵廨，鄉人咸勸徒廨以益其宅。

translations.literal: 」 Sengzhen's old house stood north of the market; before it was the postal inspector's office, and fellow townsmen all urged moving the office to enlarge his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen's old house stood north of the market, with the postal inspector's office in front; neighbors all urged moving the office to enlarge his home.

sentences.zh: 僧珍怒曰：「督郵官廨也，置立以來，便在此地，豈可徙之益吾私宅！

translations.literal: Sengzhen said angrily: "The postal inspector's office is a government building; since it was established it has stood here—how can it be moved to enlarge my private house!
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen snapped, "The postal inspector's office is a government building; it has stood here since it was built—how can you move it to enlarge my private house!

sentences.zh: 」姊適于氏，住在市西，小屋臨路，與列肆雜處，僧珍常導從鹵簿到其宅，不以爲恥。

translations.literal: 」 His elder sister had married into the Yu clan and lived west of the market in a small house facing the road, mixed among shop stalls; Sengzhen often led his full guard retinue to her home and was not ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister had married a Yu and lived west of the market in a little house on the street amid the shops; Sengzhen often led his full guard escort to her door and felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 在州百日，徵爲領軍將軍，尋加散騎常侍，給鼓吹一部，直秘書省如先。

translations.literal: After a hundred days in the province he was summoned as Commandant of the Guards; soon he was added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, given one set of ceremonial drums and pipes, and held Secretariat duty as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a hundred days in the province he was recalled as Commandant of the Guards, soon made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, given ceremonial drums and pipes, and kept his Secretariat duty as before.

sentences.zh: 僧珍有大勳，任總心膂，恩遇隆密，莫與爲比。

translations.literal: Sengzhen had great merit, held overall charge of the ruler's inner circle, and enjoyed favor so dense that none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen had great merit, stood at the heart of power, and enjoyed favor so close that none could match him.

sentences.zh: 性甚恭慎，當直禁中，盛暑不敢解衣。

translations.literal: By nature he was very respectful and cautious; when on duty in the palace, even in great heat he dared not loosen his clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply respectful and cautious by nature, on palace duty he would not loosen his clothes even in fierce summer heat.

sentences.zh: 每侍御座，屏氣鞠躬，果食未嘗舉箸。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended the imperial seat he held his breath and bowed; he never once raised his chopsticks to the fruit set before him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended the throne he held his breath and bowed low; he never once touched the fruit set before him.

sentences.zh: 嘗因醉後，取一柑食之。

translations.literal: Once, when drunk, he took a mandarin orange and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drunk, he took a mandarin and ate it.

sentences.zh: 高祖笑謂曰：「便是大有所進。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughingly said to him: "That is a great advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and said, "That is real progress.

sentences.zh: 」祿俸之外，又月給錢十萬；

translations.literal: 」 Beyond his salary he was also given a hundred thousand cash each month;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond his salary he also received a hundred thousand cash a month;

sentences.zh: 其餘賜賚不絕于時。

translations.literal: other gifts and rewards were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: and other gifts and rewards never stopped.

sentences.zh: 十年，疾病，車駕臨幸，中使醫藥，日有數四。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he fell ill; the imperial carriage visited him, and palace emissaries brought medicine several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he fell ill; the emperor came in person, and palace envoys brought medicine several times daily.

sentences.zh: 僧珍語親舊曰：「吾昔在蒙縣，熱病髮黃，當時必謂不濟，主上見語，『卿有富貴相，必當不死，尋應自差』，俄而果愈。

translations.literal: Sengzhen told relatives and friends: "I was once in Meng county with fever and turned yellow; then I surely thought I would not survive. The lord said to me, 'You have the look of wealth and rank—you will surely not die and should soon recover on your own'—and indeed I soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen told kin, "Once in Meng county I had fever and turned yellow and was sure I would die. His Majesty said, 'You have a nobleman's look—you will not die and will soon recover'—and I did.

sentences.zh: 今已富貴而復髮黃，所苦與昔正同，必不復起矣。

translations.literal: Now, having wealth and rank, I have turned yellow again; the affliction is exactly the same as before—I surely will not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am wealthy and honored I have turned yellow again with the same illness as then—I will not get up again.

sentences.zh: 」竟如其言。

translations.literal: 」 In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it was as he said.

sentences.zh: 卒於領軍府舍，時年五十八。

translations.literal: He died at the Commandant of the Guards residence, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the Commandant of the Guards residence at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 高祖卽日臨殯，詔曰：「思舊篤終，前王令典；

translations.literal: Gaozu that same day came to the mourning hall. The edict said: "Thinking fondly of the old and honoring the end—the former kings' fine model;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu came to the mourning hall that same day. The edict said, "Cherishing the old and honoring the dead is the ancient kings' model;

sentences.zh: 追榮加等，列代通規。

translations.literal: pursuing glory with added rank—the rule of every dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: adding posthumous glory is the rule of every age.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、領軍將軍、平固縣開國侯僧珍，器思淹通，識宇詳濟，竭忠盡禮，知無不爲。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commandant of the Guards, and Marquis of Pinggu district Sengzhen—his talent and thought were broad and penetrating, his knowledge and bearing detailed and accomplished; he exhausted loyalty and full ritual and knew nothing he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commandant of the Guards, and Marquis of Pinggu Sengzhen had broad talent and penetrating thought, detailed knowledge and accomplished bearing, gave exhaustive loyalty and full ritual, and left nothing undone.

sentences.zh: 與朕契闊，情兼屯泰。

translations.literal: With us in shared hardship, his feelings embraced both adversity and ease.
translations.idiomatic: He shared our hardships, his heart holding both hard times and good.

sentences.zh: 大業初構，茂勳克舉。

translations.literal: When the great undertaking was first built, splendid merit was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: When the great enterprise was first raised, he won splendid merit.

sentences.zh: 及居禁衛，朝夕盡誠。

translations.literal: When he held palace guard duty, morning and evening he gave full sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In palace guard service he gave his utmost morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 方參任台槐，式隆朝寄；

translations.literal: Just as he was to share responsibility at the high ministries and elevate the court's trust,
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to take his place among the highest ministers and bear the court's heavy trust,

sentences.zh: 奄致喪逝，傷慟于懷。

translations.literal: he suddenly met death and loss—grief filled the breast.
translations.idiomatic: he suddenly died—grief filled our hearts.

sentences.zh: 宜加優典，以隆寵命。

translations.literal: Superior rites should be added to exalt the favored mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Let superior rites be added to honor his service.

sentences.zh: 可贈驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，常侍、鼓吹、侯如故。

translations.literal: He may posthumously be granted General of Fast Cavalry and Office equaling the Three Excellencies in Staff; Cavalier Attendant, drums and pipes, and marquisate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously grant him General of Fast Cavalry and an office equal to the Three Excellencies in staff; his cavalier attendant rank, drums and pipes, and marquisate remain as before.

sentences.zh: 給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事所須，隨由備辦。

translations.literal: Eastern garden secret vessels are given, one set of court robes and one suit of clothes; whatever the funeral requires shall be prepared as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Grant eastern-garden funeral vessels, one court robe, and one suit of clothes; prepare whatever the funeral requires.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠敬侯。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Marquis Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Loyal and Respectful Marquis.

sentences.zh: 」高祖痛惜之，言爲流涕。

translations.literal: 」 Gaozu grieved deeply and spoke with tears streaming.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu grieved deeply and wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 長子峻早卒，峻子淡嗣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jun died early; Jun's son Dan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jun died young; Jun's son Dan inherited.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：張弘策敦厚慎密，呂僧珍恪勤匪懈，鄭紹叔忠誠亮藎，締構王業，三子皆有力焉。

translations.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Zhang Hongce was steady and careful, Lü Sengzhen diligent without slack, and Zheng Shaoshu loyal and bright—they helped found the royal enterprise, and all three contributed strength.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Zhang Hongce was steady and careful, Lü Sengzhen tireless in duty, and Zheng Shaoshu loyal and upright; in founding the dynasty all three gave real force.

sentences.zh: 僧珍之肅恭禁省，紹叔之造膝詭辭，蓋識爲臣之節矣。

translations.literal: Sengzhen's solemn reverence in the forbidden palace and Shaoshu's intimate counsel in subtle words at the knee—they surely knew a minister's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen's grave courtesy in the palace guard and Shaoshu's candid words at close audience show they understood a subject's duty.
